newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bond mart bids firm, trading sluggish.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bond mart bids firm, trading sluggish.

text.p: Bids on investment grade and high yield U.S. corporate bonds were firm today, although few trades took place in either market, traders said.
"Bids are unchanged to higher, but trading has been pretty thin. It looks like a lot of accounts are already closed for the holiday," said one high-grade bond trader.
In the junk market, CAI Wireless Systems bonds dropped ten points on news that the company's partnership agreement with Bell Atlantic and NYNEX Corp was suspended.
Bids for the bonds opened at 35 from their closing levels last night of 45. Bids on the bonds by midday rose to 40.
In the high grade market, spreads on some Tele-Communications Inc debt tightened by 10 basis points on rumors that the company may consider selling its 30 percent interest in Sprint Spectrum L.P.
The speculation about TCI's plans were triggered by comments made by TCI CEO John Malone on Thursday that the company plans to shift its focus on increasing the profitability of its core assets.
Sprint Spectrum, a personal communications services provider, is a joint venture between Sprint Inc and several cable companies.

Traders reported that bids on AK Steel bonds, the largest junk bond issue priced on Thursday, were up to 101 after they were freed to trade on Friday morning. The bonds were originally sold at par. Bids for other new junk issues were also stronger, they added.

In the high grade market, traders said bids on Crown Cork & Seal 100-year bonds tightend by one basis point when they were freed to trade on Friday. But bids on the company's 10-year bonds were wider by one basis point, and bids on its 30-year paper were wider by two basis points, traders said.
As of midday on Friday, the yield on the benchmark 30-year Treasury was up 18/32 to 98-30/32, yielding 6.59 percent.
